findings.ac: docs/WORKFLOW.md documents the mandatory dedicated user and the absolute-path key line
findings.title: WORKFLOW.md section is checked only by hand
findings.detail: No automated test asserts that the 'Remote gate worker' section exists, says the dedicated unprivileged user is mandatory, or contains the `command="/home/user/.local/bin/nw worker ssh-command",restrict` line. The test plan allows a manual check, so this is not blocking. A small grep test would catch the section being deleted later.

findings.title: SIGHUP cancel is not tested
findings.detail: The spec's As-shipped section says SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP all cancel a job. test_signal_mid_gate_kills_the_gate_and_sends_done only parametrizes SIGTERM and SIGINT, and test_signal_before_the_slot_is_an_error_frame only sends SIGTERM. If SIGHUP were dropped from _STOP_SIGNALS, no test would fail.

findings.ac: Two concurrent gate-jobs for the same repo_key with different base.sha each see their own base
findings.title: Concurrent-jobs test assumes at least 2 default gate slots
findings.detail: test_concurrent_jobs_see_their_own_base has each gate wait until both jobs have touched a sync file. That only works if both jobs hold a slot at the same time. If the default slot count were ever 1 (for example on a 1-CPU runner, if slots follow the CPU count), the test would hang until the gate timeout instead of failing clearly. Pinning slots: 2 in the worker config would make the test deterministic.

findings.ac: nw worker info --json prints the documented keys
findings.title: info test checks key names, not value types
findings.detail: test_info_json_keys checks the exact key set, schema, protocol, data_dir and that free_bytes is an int. It does not check version, git or uv. That is enough for the AC.

coverage_assessment.ac: Valid header+bundle runs gates and emits accepted, started, one gate frame per gate (with .log, .json, .r<n>) and done
git merge-base $NW_BASE HEAD on the worker prints the coordinator's sha
env key outside the allowlist gives an error frame with stage validate and nothing runs; a reused job_id gives stage claim
Two concurrent jobs with different base.sha for one base.name each see their own base
EOF mid-gate ends the gate and sends done interrupted; EOF during the slot wait sends done interrupted with no started
With the slot held elsewhere, the worker sends slot_wait and only then started
Exit 0 after done (pass, fail or interrupted), 3 after error
A log over 16 MiB is cut to 16 MiB and its sidecar gets truncated_bytes
have reports commit and base after the job; gc --keep-days 0 removes refs, objects and job dirs, but a live job's dir survives
nw worker info --json prints the documented keys
ssh-command execs the four allowed subcommands and refuses everything else with exit 2, running nothing
